question: Should Crabbox support jj by consuming an explicitly materialized Git-compatible revision, or should repository synchronization gain a first-class VCS adapter with native jj revision semantics?
rationale: Both approaches can address the report, but they establish materially different long-term contracts, complexity, caching semantics, and maintenance obligations that source inspection alone cannot choose.

options.title: Define a VCS adapter
options.body: Introduce a generic snapshot and manifest boundary, retain Git as the default adapter, and implement jj revision selection through a dedicated adapter.

options.title: Require Git materialization
options.body: Document and validate a supported workflow where users materialize the intended jj revision into colocated Git state before Crabbox synchronizes it.

options.title: Defer native support
options.body: Keep Git as the only supported repository model and improve diagnostics so jj users receive an actionable unsupported-workspace error instead of silently syncing the wrong content.

recommendation.title: Define a VCS adapter
recommendation.body: Introduce a generic snapshot and manifest boundary, retain Git as the default adapter, and implement jj revision selection through a dedicated adapter.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice affects the established synchronization contract and cross-cutting CLI architecture, making the broad recent repository contributor the best available decision owner.
